a11y-gate.why: Accessibility failures are cross-cutting and are easiest to introduce when a visual change appears finished. This skill is a completion gate so accessible names, keyboard operation, semantics, contrast, motion, and streaming announcements are verified before visual polish is mistaken for product readiness.
useCases: Review a new React, Tauri, or Flutter screen before completion
Audit keyboard focus, screen-reader output, contrast, or reduced motion
Verify accessible status updates for streaming agent and tool events
a11y-gate.notFor: It does not replace platform visual review or runtime verification; pair it with tauri-ui-review, flutter-golden-ui, and hybrid-runtime-verification.

a2ui-surface-contract.why: A2UI is deliberately a projection protocol. Keeping execution authority out of the renderer prevents generated UI, approval components, and action continuations from bypassing UAR governance.
useCases: Render typed agent-generated forms or components
Continue an A2UI action after restart
Handle unknown component types, approval state, or cancellation consistently
a2ui-surface-contract.notFor: Do not use it to select models, execute tools, or make policy decisions in a client.

agent-runtime-security.why: Tool descriptions, model output, transport metadata, and client claims are all untrusted. The skill establishes one governed sequence for trust resolution, schema validation, effect classification, authorization, confirmation, bounded execution, and immutable audit.
useCases: Add or review an MCP-backed tool
Implement approval, cancellation, timeout, or output limits
Validate JWT/JWKS identity and tenant isolation around agent runs
agent-runtime-security.notFor: It does not define application-specific policy. Put roles, tenant rules, and release boundaries in the project policy overlay.

agui-event-contract.why: Streaming clients reconnect, duplicate messages, and observe partial failure. A versioned, replayable AG-UI envelope makes event application deterministic instead of inferring run state from prose or connection lifetime.
useCases: Expose UAR events over SSE
Resume a run from Last-Event-ID
Test duplicate, out-of-order, unknown, denied, or cancelled events
agui-event-contract.notFor: It does not define visual components; use a2ui-surface-contract or content-block-ui for rendering.

anonymized-replica.why: Removing names is not anonymization. The skill preserves scenario behavior and referential shape while explicitly controlling direct identifiers, quasi-identifiers, secrets, free text, provenance, and reproducibility.
useCases: Create a production-shaped POC dataset
Build deterministic certification fixtures
Review de-identification and re-identification risk
anonymized-replica.notFor: Do not use it as permission to copy production transcripts, credentials, documents, or raw client notes.

axum-agent-gateway.why: The browser must not become an agent runtime or authorization boundary. The Axum gateway derives verified identity, applies policy, submits bounded UAR commands, and streams typed results through a server-controlled boundary.
useCases: Add authenticated run and cancellation endpoints
Stream AG-UI/A2UI events from UAR to a web client
Enforce tenant derivation, idempotency, policy denial, and slow-consumer behavior
axum-agent-gateway.notFor: Do not expose raw MCP execution, caller-selected tenants, or provider routing through the gateway.

build-branded-docusaurus.why: A documentation site is a publication boundary, not a folder copied to the web. The skill separates public sources from private evidence, preserves brand and accessibility contracts, and requires deterministic search, sanitization, links, builds, screenshots, and deployment checks.
useCases: Create or extend a Docusaurus product portal
Publish architecture and API guidance to GitHub Pages
Add Mermaid, local search, container delivery, or publication sanitization
build-branded-docusaurus.notFor: Do not publish raw wikis, session logs, credentials, personal information, or generated build output as source.

client-rag.why: Retrieval is derived application state and must preserve privacy-class boundaries. The skill fixes embedding dimensions, per-tier stores, local execution, provenance, and a single retrieval facade so each feature cannot invent an incompatible vector pipeline.
useCases: Search conversations, notes, or agent memory on-device
Add pgvector, sqlite-vec, HNSW, BM25, or hybrid retrieval
Build embed-on-write and idempotent backfill workflows
client-rag.notFor: Cloud RAG is a separate design and privacy review; vault vectors never enter server-synced tables.

content-block-ui.why: One exhaustive discriminated union keeps Rust, Dart, TypeScript, A2UI, and AG-UI renderers aligned. Compile-time exhaustiveness and one renderer per variant prevent silent loss of new agent-output types.
useCases: Render chat text, thinking, tools, skills, citations, artifacts, or media
Add a new ContentBlock variant across Rust, Flutter, and React
Review streaming, disclosure, accessibility, and status transitions
content-block-ui.notFor: Do not hand-edit generated language mirrors or replace the exhaustive dispatcher with ad hoc conditionals.

dependency-pin-discipline.why: A generator must reproduce the same stack on every machine. Exact pins, a single version authority, and rationale comments prevent silent drift and make coordinated code-generation dependency changes reviewable.
useCases: Add or upgrade Cargo, npm, pnpm, Flutter, Gradle, or toolchain dependencies
Resolve analyzer or code-generation version conflicts
Audit version literals and lockfile consistency
dependency-pin-discipline.notFor: It does not choose architecture or certify a release; it governs how selected versions are recorded and moved.

deploy-hybrid-agentic-stack.why: Hybrid applications share one typed service layer but have several delivery shapes. The skill makes deployment profiles explicit while preventing browsers, mobile clients, and generated apps from duplicating infrastructure or bypassing governance.
useCases: Plan local, web, realtime, authenticated, or full-agentic deployment
Add Axum asset delivery, containers, Kubernetes, GitOps, or BYOK
Verify selected services from a clean checkout through a public workflow
deploy-hybrid-agentic-stack.notFor: Do not enable every service by default or create a second image/catalog pipeline inside a consumer.

domain-glossary-service.why: Prompts are a poor place to hide vocabulary rules. A versioned glossary gives humans, retrieval, policy, and agents a deterministic terminology contract while keeping customer-specific language in project overlays.
useCases: Normalize canonical terms and synonyms
Map vocabulary to entities or policy actions
Handle deprecation, locale fallback, ambiguity, and revision pinning
domain-glossary-service.notFor: Do not place customer names, URLs, roles, or private terminology in the reusable Builder package.

entity-graph-web-shell.why: Normalized entity state must converge across views without making components aware of transports. PEM owns durable application state, hooks expose intent, and Axum owns remote effects and verified identity.
useCases: Build a React shell over PEM and PGlite
Register entity transports and normalized cross-view updates
Test offline replay, projection recovery, and tenant denial
entity-graph-web-shell.notFor: Components must not call fetch, IPC, raw stores, or UAR directly.

flutter-golden-ui.why: Widget correctness is visual and stateful, so helper-level unit coverage cannot prove it. Deterministic goldens in both themes plus the live Flutter inspector provide reviewable evidence at the public widget boundary.
useCases: Complete a new or changed Flutter widget or screen
Capture light/dark visual states with production tokens
Review overflow, font loading, animation, semantics, and device sizing
flutter-golden-ui.notFor: Do not update goldens merely to make a failing test green; inspect and approve the intended visual change.

hybrid-design-tokens.why: Hand-maintained Flutter and web themes inevitably diverge. One typed token source and generated outputs turn cross-surface visual parity from a convention into a mechanically verifiable contract.
useCases: Add or change color, typography, spacing, radius, motion, or breakpoints
Generate Tailwind/CSS and Flutter token outputs together
Audit semantic naming and light/dark contrast
hybrid-design-tokens.notFor: Do not place raw color or spacing literals in components or hand-edit generated token outputs.

hybrid-runtime-verification.why: Compilation cannot prove startup, persistence, native symbol binding, model loading, or a real user workflow. The skill defines evidence levels and forces physical-device verification when host checks cannot observe the failure class.
useCases: Validate a release, profile, platform baseline, or inference lane
Prove clean-checkout build, launch, persistence, and public workflow
Record physical Android or iOS certification evidence
hybrid-runtime-verification.notFor: Build-only, mocked, emulator-only, or source-inspection results must not be reported as a working physical-device release.

karpathy-progress-memory.why: Long-running work loses decisions and repeats failures when only transcripts retain context. Compact evidence records preserve intent, delta, proof, failure, and the next experiment without turning every tool call into permanent noise.
useCases: Record a task or phase boundary
Prepare a cross-harness handoff
Promote a verified reusable lesson after a failure or design decision
karpathy-progress-memory.notFor: Do not store secrets, raw transcripts, unsupported claims, or private memory in public repository documentation.

legacy-app-embed.why: An embedded legacy application is an independently deployed, potentially hostile system. A versioned, capability-limited bridge prevents postMessage convenience from becoming an identity, tenant, policy, or runtime bypass.
useCases: Embed a frozen SSR application in a governed shell
Define origin, source-window, version, and correlation checks
Test replay, navigation, reload, timeout, and malformed messages
legacy-app-embed.notFor: Never send credentials, trusted tenant IDs, policy decisions, database access, or raw runtime handles through the bridge.

local-inference-lanes.why: Engine selection is per device while execution lane selection is per turn. Separating those concepts behind InferenceProvider prevents a false universal mobile engine, unsafe cloud fallback, and platform-specific types leaking into application code.
useCases: Add or debug LiteRT-LM, MLX, llama.cpp, or WebLLM
Implement model download, checksums, revision pins, or RAM preflight
Route cloud, local, and UAR turns without silent fallback
local-inference-lanes.notFor: Do not certify a local lane from compilation; model loading and native bridges require real-device evidence.

mini-app-module.why: A folder of components is not a removable product boundary. A versioned module manifest makes routes, entities, capabilities, policy actions, events, and migrations explicit so the shell can validate, isolate, lazy-load, upgrade, or disable the module.
useCases: Add a governed applet to a web shell
Register routes, entities, navigation, capabilities, or migrations
Test isolation, permission denial, lazy-load failure, and disablement
mini-app-module.notFor: Do not allow modules to import each other's internal stores, components, or transports.

mobile-navigation.why: Platform sniffing creates two navigation trees for a distinction that does not exist at phone width. One destination model with a width-driven bottom-bar-to-rail transition follows both platform conventions and preserves router authority.
useCases: Add top-level Flutter, React, Tauri, or PWA destinations
Switch navigation chrome at responsive breakpoints
Audit safe areas, router-derived selection, and accessible landmarks
mobile-navigation.notFor: Do not use OS checks or user-agent detection to choose top-level navigation placement.

orchestrate-prometheus-application.why: Complex application work needs explicit scenario classification, authority boundaries, bounded phases, independent criticism, and public-boundary evidence. The skill coordinates those artifacts without replacing Prometheus lifecycle authority.
useCases: Plan a composite hybrid, SaaS, automation, native-agent, or documentation build
Select relevant skills, references, harnesses, and producer/critic roles
Run Feynman, KBD, PMPO, verification, and retention loops coherently
orchestrate-prometheus-application.notFor: Builder activation aids must not pause, resume, lease, hand off, or mutate Prometheus KBD state.

peer-profile-sync.why: User-owned profile and learned-personalization data has a different authority model from shared relational data. A local-only Loro vault with authenticated device pairing makes server exclusion structural rather than a best-effort filter.
useCases: Synchronize private profile data between a user's devices
Implement pairing, revocation, CRDT convergence, or encrypted export
Keep agent-learned personal facts out of server sync and cloud persistence
peer-profile-sync.notFor: Shared tenant data belongs in the relational lane; do not weaken the vault because a feature needs server persistence.

pem-local-first.why: A query cache models requests, while a local-first application models durable entities and pending mutations. PEM provides one normalized entity graph over local stores so views converge without a second freshness authority.
useCases: Add an entity type, transport, local projection, or optimistic mutation
Persist conversations across PGlite, pglite-oxide, or SQLite
Surface queue and dead-letter state through reactive views
pem-local-first.notFor: Do not introduce TanStack Query, SWR, Apollo cache, a second replay queue, or direct component transports.

persona-scoped-agent.why: A persona is behavior configuration, not authorization. Pinning persona instructions, tools, retrieval scopes, budgets, policy revision, and eligibility prevents client-selected roles or prompt text from granting capabilities.
useCases: Build role-aware or mode-specific assistants
Apply persona-specific retrieval and tool allowlists
Enforce prepare-only or named-human release boundaries
persona-scoped-agent.notFor: Do not trust a persona or role supplied by the client, and do not encode authorization solely in a system prompt.

reference-ui-fidelity.why: A supplied design is an acceptance oracle, not loose inspiration. Inventorying every route, state, theme, and form factor before coding prevents a polished shell from hiding missing product surfaces.
useCases: Implement from Figma, OpenDesign, HTML prototypes, screenshots, or mood boards
Build a route/state/theme/form-factor coverage matrix
Run screenshot convergence while preserving real architecture
reference-ui-fidelity.notFor: If no authoritative reference exists, do not invent one and claim fidelity.

sync-doctrine.why: Most sync defects begin by assigning data to the wrong authority or privacy lane. The doctrine forces an explicit relational, CRDT, or event-log choice plus privacy class before transport and UI details obscure the decision.
useCases: Add synced tables, subscriptions, offline writes, lookup bundles, or onboarding loads
Design scoped replication and durable operation queues
Review privacy-class refusal, auth re-checks, and thin-client fallback
sync-doctrine.notFor: Do not mirror the server database, apply CRDTs to every row, or create parallel write queues.

tauri-custom-titlebar.why: Removing native window chrome transfers platform behavior and accessibility responsibility to the application. The skill makes surface gating, control placement, dragging, web safety, and accessible controls explicit.
useCases: Build branded Tauri window chrome
Implement drag regions and platform-correct window controls
Prevent Tauri-only APIs from crashing a shared web bundle
tauri-custom-titlebar.notFor: Do not render desktop window controls in a browser, PWA, or Flutter mobile surface.

tauri-ui-review.why: Responsive and themed defects are invisible from one developer viewport. A fixed screenshot matrix and layer-contract review makes visual completion repeatable and catches stock-template styling, overflow, missing states, and architecture shortcuts.
useCases: Complete a changed React or Tauri screen
Review 320, 768, 1024, and 1440 pixel widths in both themes
Compare implemented states with an approved reference and accessibility gate
tauri-ui-review.notFor: A single screenshot, dev-server load, or polished route cannot certify the full product surface.
